Daily Quiz.question: ১) A literary term used to describe a satire or comedy is called -
Daily Quiz.exp:
• A literary term used to describe a satire or comedy is called farce.
A farce is a literary genre and type of comedy that makes use of highly exaggerated and funny situations aimed at entertaining the audience. Farce is also a subcategory of dramatic comedy, which is different from other forms of comedy as it only aims at making the audience laugh.

- Satire is a literary device for the artful ridicule of folly or vice as a means of exposing or correcting it.
- Comedy is generally defined as a literary work that is written to amuse or entertain a reader.
- Hymn is a religious song or poem in praise of God.
- Allegory is a literary term in which one story is told in the guise of another story.
- Parable - an allegorical story usually containing a moral lesson

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman & literarydevices.net

Daily Quiz.question: ২) Richardson's Pamela is an example of -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Epistolary Novel 
অনেকটা চিঠির মতো করে লেখা এই উপন্যাসগুলো।
- A novel told through in the form of letters.
- The narrative of this type of novel is carried forward by letters written by one or more of the characters of that novel. 

Example: Pamela by Richardson.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৩) ______ is an implicit or indirect reference to another work of literature.
Daily Quiz.exp:
Allusion is an implicit or indirect reference to another work of literature, a historical or mythical person or event.

Examples:
‘The winged boy I knew;
But who wast thou, O happy, happy dove?’
(Keats: “Ode to Psyche”)
The “winged boy” is an allusion to Cupid, the god of love.
''Not half so fixed the Trojan could remain,
While Anna begged and Dido raged in vain'' is another example of allusion.
(Pope: The Rape of the Lock)

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) The renaissance began in____
Daily Quiz.exp:
Though the renaissance began in 1453, it's effect on English life and literature was left after 1500.
For this reason, it is generally accepted that the Renaissance Period began at the beginning of the 16th century and continued till the Restoration in 1660.
The Renaissance Literary period began in 1500.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৫) Hyperbole can be-
Daily Quiz.option1: ক) positive as well as negative.
Daily Quiz.exp:
Hyperbole is an exaggerated statement or an extreme overstatement.

Here, “Ten thousand saw I at a glance” - is an example of hyperbole.
- Hyperbole used to create strong emotional response. 
- It can be positive as well as negative. 
- It can be a source of laughter. 
- It also can be a bitter criticism. 

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৬) Which one is an example of famous mock-epic?
Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) The Rape of the Lock
Daily Quiz.exp:
Mock-epic:
A narrative poem that aims at mockery and laughter by using almost all the characteristic features of an epic but for a trivial subject.
- Pope's well-known poem, 'The Rape of the Lock' is a famous mock-epic.
- The grand treatment of a low subject produces hilarious laughter and makes the story ridiculous. 

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৭) Which is the shortest period of English literature?
Daily Quiz.exp:
English Literature Periods:
450 - 1066 :- The Old English Period
1066 - 1500 :- The Middle English Period
1500 - 1660 :- The Renaissance Period
1660 - 1785 :- The Neoclassical Period
1798 - 1832 :- Romantic Period
1832 - 1901 :- Victorian Period

The Neo-classical Period is divided into three shorter periods:
• The Restoration Period (1660-1700),
• The Augustan Period (1700-1745) and
• The Age of Sensibility (1745-1785/1798).

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৮) What kind of writing is Milton's ‘Areopagitica’?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Pamphlet:
An argumentative writing in prose on controversial issue of a particular time.
- It is written to favour a side of the controversy and suggest a solution. 
- Milton's ‘Areopagitica’ is an example of it. 

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) "Who hath not seen thee oft amid thy store?" is an example of-
Daily Quiz.exp:
A figure of speech in which lifeless objects or ideas are given imaginary life known as Personification.
Examples-
''And Joy, whose hand is ever at his lips Bidding adieu'' (Keats: 'Ode on Melancholy')
- here 'Joy' has been imagined as a living person.
"Who hath not seen thee oft amid thy store?" (Keats: 'To Autumn')

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) Shakespeare lived during the reign of -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Elizabethan Age (1558-1603):
- This age is named after 'Queen Elizabeth I' who reigned over England from 1558 to 1603.
- This is called the Golden Age of English literature.
- Christopher Marlowe, William Shakespeare, Thomas Kyd, Thomas Norton, Francis Bacon etc are famous literary figure of this period.

William Shakespeare is the greatest English dramatist.
He was born on 23 April, 1564 AD, and died on 23 April, 1616 AD.
His Birthplace is Stratford Avon. He is often called the Bard of Avon.
Shakespearean period belongs to '1590-1616'.
He wrote 37 plays and 154 sonnets.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১১) Metaphor is a comparison between-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Metaphor is a comparison between two unlike entities.
- Metaphor, figure of speech that implies comparison between two unlike entities, as distinguished from simile, an explicit comparison signalled by the words like or as.
-Many critics regard the making of metaphors as a system of thought antedating or bypassing logic.

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ১২) Petrarchan Sonnet is divided into -
Daily Quiz.option1: ক) two quatrains and one sestet
Daily Quiz.option2: খ) an octave and a sestet
Daily Quiz.option3: গ) three quatrains and a couplet
Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) two sestet and a couplet
Daily Quiz.exp:
Sonnet: A lyric poem of fourteen iambic pentameter lines.

- Italian or Petrarchan Sonnet: Named for the Italian Renaissance lyrical poet Francesco Petrarch, this sonnet pattern consists of an eight-line Octave with the rhyme scheme ABBA ABBA, followed by a six-line Sestet that follows one of two rhyme schemes, CDE CDE or CDC CDC.

-------------------------
- English or Shakespearean Sonnet: Named for William Shakespeare and a variation of the Italian sonnet, this sonnet pattern consists of three four-line Quatrains and a concluding couplet with the rhyme scheme ABAB CDCD EFEF GG.

- Spenserian: Named for the English poet Edmund Spenser, a contemporary of William Shakespeare, this sonnet pattern is a variation of the Shakespearean sonnet and features a more challenging rhyme scheme, ABAB BCBC CDCD EE.

- Miltonic: Named for the English poet John Milton, this sonnet pattern is considered an evolution of the Shakespearean sonnet. Milton used the Petrarchan form as well and expanded the traditional limits of rhyme and length in composing many of his sonnets. In addition, Miltonic sonnets often address themes of internal struggles and conflict rather than external world themes.

- Occitan Sonnets:  These sonnets appeared in Italy in the 13th century with ABABABAB, CDCDCD rhyme scheme and were written for singing.

- Caudate Sonnets: These sonnets comprise a total of fourteen lines with a coda. Francesco Berni first wrote these poems and popularized them.

- Curtal Sonnets: Written by Manley Hopkins, these sonnets comprise eleven lines with amendments to Petrarchan standards.


Source: literarydevices.net (Link)

Daily Quiz.question: ১৩) A kind of funeral prayer is-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Requiem
- A musical composition for the mass (A kind of funeral prayer) of a dead person). 
- It has religious fervour. 
- Mozart was a famous composer of requiems.
- William Croft, Thomas Morley, Thomas Tomkins, Christopher Wood are some of the many English requiem composers. 

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১৪) The writer of the Victorian age is-
Daily Quiz.exp:
George Eliot is a Victorian writer.
- Mary Ann Evans is the real name of George Eliot.

- Lord Byron, Jane Austen, John Keats were writers from the Romantic Age.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৫) Which one is an example of Romantic Comedy?
Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) The Way of the World
Daily Quiz.exp:
Romantic Comedy
A form of comedy which deals with love, often love at first sight, as its main theme. 
- It starts with some problems that make the union of the lovers difficult. 
- However, the problems are finally solved and the play ends with the lovers happy union.
- Shakespeare's 'As you like it' is a romantic comedy. 

 Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) ________ ends suddenly with the sense of incompleteness.
Daily Quiz.exp:
Short story 
A short fictional narrative in prose (of six to ten thousand words) that can be read in one sitting. 
- It starts abruptly, rises to a climax and ends suddenly with the sense of incompleteness. 
- The incident in it is invented instead of being an account of on event that actually happened. 
- Short stories are also called Short-fiction.  

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question:
১৭) "O wind,
If Winter comes, can spring be far behind?" Here the 'O wind' feres to-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Apostrophe:
An address to someone absent or something abstract as if the person or the thing were present. 
It is often introduced by the exclamation "O". 
- Shelly makes use of Apostrophe in "Ode to the West Wind" at least seven times. 
Here is one of them: 
"O wind,
If Winter comes, can spring be far behind?"

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১৮) The peak of importance in a play or in a story is called-
Daily Quiz.exp:
The peak of importance in a play or story is called climax.
- It this the point at which the rise of action ends and the fall of action begins.
For example: Antigone’s death is the climax of Oedipus.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১৯) Robert Browning was a poet of ______ age.
Daily Quiz.exp:
Robert Browning is a Victorian Poet.

• A list of writers of the 'Victorian Age':
- Charles Dickens,
- Thomas Hardy,
- Matthew Arnold,
- Lord Alfred Tennyson,
- Robert Browning,
- George Eliot,
- Samuel Butler etc.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ২০) Which literary term best suits ‘Pilgrim’s Progress’?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Allegory is a literary term in which one story is told in the guise of another story.
- In other words, an allegory is a story of double meaning.
- Its author comments upon some persons or events of his age under disguised names. 
- It may be both in prose and in verse. 
- Bunyan’s 'Pilgrim’s Progress' is a well-known allegory in prose which deals with the Christian notion of a soul’s salvation.
- Dryden’s Absalom and Architople is a political allegory.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman
